stemMd: The second passage would most directly oppose the claim that

options.label: A
options.textMd: discretionary panels can make unjustified distinctions.

options.label: B
options.textMd: a lottery may be useful within a fair system.

options.label: C
options.textMd: relevant differences can justify different priorities.

options.label: D
options.textMd: an impartial lottery is sufficient to ensure fairness of the programme as a whole.

options.label: E
options.textMd: losing a lottery can be disappointing.

explanationMd: The second author distinguishes fairness at allocation from fairness across the programme. Equal odds do not remove barriers to applying or attending, so the lottery alone is insufficient.

distractorRationale.c: The first permits this and the second need not deny it.
distractorRationale.e: The second does not dispute that observation.
distractorRationale.a: The second does not defend such panels.
